title: Shared components and sandboxed extensions translate with the app's i18next
summary: Extensions installed from a link run in a sealed-off frame, and until now Seed Bible's ready-made buttons (like **Close**) crashed there and couldn't show the app's language. This PR sends the app's words and language into that frame, so those buttons work and follow the app's language, including right-to-left Arabic. In the app itself nothing should look different: the first section checks that on the preview, and the second section tries the example extension, which needs someone comfortable running commands on their own computer.

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Use the **Open the preview build** button above, in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a computer. If the page shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload.

setup.title: Make sure you're seeing the new version
setup.body: The app saves a copy of itself in your browser. Do a hard refresh once: **Ctrl+Shift+R** on Windows, **Cmd+Shift+R** on Mac. A private/incognito window also gives you a clean start.

setup.title: Know where the language setting is
setup.body: Several tests switch the app's language. Open **Settings** and use the **Language** setting. Remember how to get back: English is listed as **English**. Start every section in English.

sections.title: The app itself still speaks your language (on the preview)
sections.intro: The PR changed where the app's buttons get their words from. Nothing here should look different from the live app.

tests.title: Close buttons are still labeled "Close" in English
steps: Open **Settings**.
Rest the mouse pointer on the **×** button that closes the Settings window, without clicking, and wait a second.
Click the **×**.
expected: A small tooltip says **Close**.
The Settings window closes.

tests.title: The search box's clear button still works
steps: Open **Settings**.
In the search box at the top of Settings, type `language`.
Rest the pointer on the **×** at the end of the search box, then click it.
expected: The tooltip says **Clear search**.
Clicking it empties the search box and the full list of settings comes back.

tests.title: Switching to Spanish changes the app's buttons too
steps: In **Settings** → **Language**, choose Spanish (listed as **Español** or **Spanish**).
Rest the pointer on the **×** that closes Settings.
Type something in the Settings search box and rest the pointer on its **×**.
Close Settings and look around the reader.
expected: The app's menus and labels are in Spanish.
The close button's tooltip says **Cerca** (an existing translation mistake for "Close", known and left for the translators, not caused by this PR).
The search box's clear button says **Borrar búsqueda**.

tests.title: The Bible translation and book pickers are in the chosen language
tests.before: The app is still in Spanish from the previous test.
steps: In the reader, open the picker where you choose a Bible translation (click the translation name at the top of the reader).
Look at the options for sorting or filtering the list of translations.
Open the picker where you choose a book and chapter.
expected: The translation list and its sorting options (in English these are **All translations**, **Popular translations** and so on) are in Spanish.
The book picker's labels (in English **All Books**, **Old Testament**, **New Testament**) are in Spanish.
Nothing is blank or shows code-like text such as `all-translations`.

tests.title: Arabic lays the app out right to left
steps: In **Settings** → **Language**, choose Arabic (listed as **العربية** or **Arabic**).
Look at the Settings window and the reader. Rest the pointer on the **×** that closes Settings.
expected: Menus and labels are in Arabic and read from right to left (the layout is mirrored).
The close button's tooltip shows Arabic text, not **Close**.

tests.title: Back in English, everything is in English again
steps: Switch the language back to **English**.
Open and close Settings, and open the translation picker.
expected: Everything is in English and laid out left to right again, with **Close** on the close button's tooltip.

tests.title: On a phone, the bottom sheets still open and close
tests.why: The sheet that slides up from the bottom on phones is one of the shared parts whose wording source changed.
steps: Open the preview on a phone, or make your computer's browser window as narrow as it goes and reload.
Tap a verse in the reader, so the verse options slide up from the bottom.
Close the sheet with its close button or by tapping outside it.
Open the book picker and close it with the **×** at its top left.
expected: The sheet opens and closes normally, with labels in English.
The book picker shows the heading **Books** and closes with its **×**.

sections.title: A sandboxed extension speaks the app's language (on your own computer)
sections.intro: Needs someone comfortable copying commands into a terminal. If that's not you, mark these tests **Skip**. The example extension used here isn't on the preview: it only runs from a developer's computer.

setup.title: Install the tools once
setup.body: You need Git, Node.js and pnpm 10. Follow the first steps of the Seed Bible README (Git; Node.js through nvm with `nvm install latest` and `nvm use latest`; then pnpm with `corepack use pnpm@latest-10`): https://github.com/HelloAOLab/seed-bible#readme

setup.title: Get this pull request's code
setup.body: In a terminal, run these one at a time.
setup.code:
git clone https://github.com/HelloAOLab/seed-bible.git
cd seed-bible
git fetch origin pull/2175/head:pr-2175
git checkout pr-2175
pnpm install

setup.title: Build the packages the extension uses
setup.body: Still in the `seed-bible` folder. This can take a few minutes.

setup.title: Start the example extension
setup.body: This starts Seed Bible on your computer with the example extension ready to install, and opens it in your browser. The first start can take a few minutes. Leave the terminal open while you test. When Seed Bible asks whether to install the extension, agree. Sign in if it asks you to.

tests.title: The extension's pane opens with its text and a Close button
tests.why: Before this PR, a shared button inside a sandboxed extension crashed its frame.
steps: In the Seed Bible window that `pnpm dev` opened, open the toolbar's **More** menu and choose **My Example Tool**.
expected: A pane opens showing an orange banner, the greeting **Hello, World**, the line **The greeting is shown once.**, a **Send a request with the sensitive settings** button and a **Close** button.
No error message or empty pane.

tests.title: The count line changes wording with the number
tests.why: The extension's own text now supports singular and plural forms.
steps: Open **Settings** → **Extensions**, open the example extension, and set **Repeat count** to `3`.
Close the pane if it's open, then open **My Example Tool** again.
expected: The greeting appears three times in a row.
The line under it says **The greeting is shown 3 times.**

tests.title: The pane's Close button closes the pane
steps: With the pane open, click its **Close** button.
expected: The pane closes.

tests.title: In Spanish, the pane's Close button uses the app's Spanish word
steps: Switch the app's language to Spanish (**Español**) in **Settings** → **Language**.
Open the toolbar's **More** menu and choose the example tool (now **Mi herramienta de ejemplo**).
Click the pane's close button.
expected: The pane's close button says **Cerca** (the app's current Spanish word for "Close": a known translation mistake, not a failure of this test).
The banner is in Spanish. The count line stays in English, because the example extension has no Spanish for it.
Clicking the button closes the pane.

tests.title: In Arabic, the pane is right to left
steps: Switch the app's language to Arabic (**العربية**).
Open the example tool from the toolbar's **More** menu.
expected: The pane's content is laid out right to left (text lines up on the right).
The close button shows the app's Arabic word **يغلق**, not **Close** or **Cerca**.
The banner is in Arabic.

tests.title: An open pane follows a language change
tests.why: The PR sends the app's words to the extension again whenever the language changes.
steps: Open the example tool's pane, so it stays open on the side.
Without closing it, switch the app's language to **English** in **Settings** → **Language**, then close Settings.
Look at the pane.
expected: Without reopening, the pane's close button now says **Close** and its text reads left to right.
If you can't change the language without the pane closing, note that and reopen it: it should show **Close**.

notCovered: How large an extension's download is: the PR shrinks a sandboxed extension that uses shared buttons from about 8 MB to about 100 KB. That's checked by automated tests and the build, not by hand.
A first visit where an extension starts before the app's language has finished loading: the PR resends the words once they arrive. That timing is hard to reproduce by hand and has automated tests.
Changes for extension authors: the `sb.i18n.t` function, the testing helpers, the new-extension template, the new lint rule for translation keys containing `:`, and the documentation.
Link pictures on playlist cards: a helper they use moved to a new file without changing what it does.
